practice.title: PHASE 13 RAPID-FIRE
practice.afterTopic: Verifying generated code: the discipline that matters
items: Stop reason? Why generation ended; the only reliable truncation detector.
max_tokens stop? Truncated â€” raise budget, shrink prompt, or split the task. Never retry identically.
Why normalize provider responses? So a vendor shape change fails in CI, not production.
Why capability flags, not lowest-common-denominator? You would erase prompt caching and schema controls.
Native schema mode? Provider constrains decoding to satisfy your JSON Schema.
Tool-call-as-output? When no native schema mode: one tool whose parameters are your schema.
Why a tolerant JSON parser? Models emit fences, preambles, trailing commas, and prose.
Why an insufficient_evidence branch? A schema with no escape hatch forces the model to invent.
Repair loop, max attempts? One. Two at most, and never resend the whole original context.
Cross-field business rules in a schema? Impossible â€” enforce deterministically after parsing.
SSE vs WebSockets? Unidirectional, plain HTTP, auto-reconnect; use fetch + reader for POST bodies.
Proxy breaks streaming? Buffering â€” set proxy_buffering off, no-transform, X-Accel-Buffering: no.
Keep partial output on abort? Yes â€” mark it partial; deleting the user's work is unforgivable.
TTFB budget separate from total? Yes â€” patience ends at first byte, not at completion.
Retry classification? 429/5xx/connect yes; 4xx, refusal, truncation, mid-stream timeout no.
Backoff jitter? Full jitter, always â€” without it you build a thundering herd.
Retries vs semaphore? Prefer admission control; retries add tail latency exactly when you are overloaded.
Who owns conversation state? The server. Providers are stateless.
Quadratic cost in chat? Resending full history every turn is O(nÂ²); window or summarize.
Compaction trigger? Projected next-request tokens over a fraction of the window, minus output reserve.
Summary style? Factual and entity-focused, cumulative â€” state, not narrative.
Prompt anatomy? Role, context, task, constraints, output contract â€” stable prefix first.
Why stable prefix first? Cache effectiveness and instruction salience.
Few-shot beats adjectives because? Examples specify the decision boundary; adjectives gesture.
Which few-shot cases? Typical, hardest edge, and a negative case.
Prompt versioning? Version is code, with a changelog and an identity recorded per request.
What is a "recipe"? Prompt + model + schema + params + retrieval config, bound by one id.
Why multiple samples per eval case? Hosted models are not bit-stable; compare distributions.
Hallucination reduction? Retrieve real evidence, force a no-answer path, verify citations resolve.
Cheap hallucination check? Cited numbers must appear in the cited source.
Refusal: never retry? Correct â€” it is either a policy block or your own prompt's doing.
Truncation: how detected? stop_reason, not string heuristics.
Instruction conflict? Contradictory rules, or examples that violate rules; fix by auditing, not hoping.
Naive RAG's main weakness? Retrieval quality, not generation quality. Fix retrieval first.
Embedding choice? Benchmark 2â€“4 candidates on your own labelled queries; pick on recall then cost.
Changing the embedding model? Full reindex. Dual-index migration, shadow, cut over, keep v1 warm.
Chunk by tokens, not characters? Always â€” character sizing mis-sizes with code and non-Latin text.
Parent-child retrieval? Embed small chunks, return the parent section; precision without losing context.
Table chunking? One row per chunk, with the header row prepended every time.
ef_search? The runtime recall/latency dial; set it from a measured recall target.

export async function filteredSearch(
  q: Float32Array, tenantId: string, opts: { tags?: string[]; k: number },
): Promise<SearchHit[]> {
  const over = opts.tags && opts.tags.length > 0 ? opts.k * 8 : opts.k;
  const rows = await sql`

     ${opts.tags && opts.tags.length > 0 ? sql`AND heading_path && ${opts.tags}` : sql``}
     ORDER BY embedding <=> ${toPgVector(q)}::vector
     LIMIT ${over}`;
  const filtered =
